newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo to sell Teck 40 pct in Stone Boy project.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo to sell Teck 40 pct in Stone Boy project.

text.p: Sumitomo Metal Mining Co Ltd said on Tuesday that its U.S. subsidiary had agreed to sell part of its stake in the Alaskan Stone Boy mining project to Canada's Teck Corp.

Sumitomo Metal said in a statement that Teck Corp would pay about $28 million for a 40 percent stake in Stone Boy Inc, a unit set up to explore gold, lead and zinc in a 16,000 sq km area east of Fairbanks, Alaska.

The Stone Boy project was launched by an international consortium which included Canada's Watts, Griffis and McOuat, and Noranda Inc. But since 1995, Sumitomo's U.S. unit, Sumitomo Metal Mining Arizona Inc has been the sole operator.
It plans to spend about $5.5 million this year to investigate the Liese gold mine in the Pogo area by exploration drilling at 40 sites, each testing depths of 40,000 feet, the statement said.
